requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation maps to code in `src/outline/rust.rs` and to a test in `src/outline/tests.rs`.

**Outline nodes for the listed item kinds.** The `KINDS` table in `src/outline/rust.rs`, reached from `static[PROFILE]`, maps every kind the requirement lists:
- Functions and methods: `function_item` and `function_signature_item` map to `fn`.
- Types: `struct_item`, `enum_item` and `union_item` map to `struct`, `enum` and `union`.
- Traits and impls: `trait_item` and `impl_item` map to `trait` and `impl`.
- Modules and macros: `mod_item` maps to `mod`, and `macro_definition` maps to `macro`.
- Constants, statics and type aliases: `const_item`, `static_item`, `type_item` and `associated_type` map to `const`, `static` and `type`.
- Extern blocks: `foreign_mod_item` maps to `extern`.
- `extern_crate_declaration` maps to `extern-crate`, which the requirement does not list.

**Tests for node kinds.** `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` in `src/outline/tests.rs` asserts the selector of every one of these kinds. It checks `macro[make]`, `union[U]`, `enum[E]`, `const[C]`, `static[S]`, `type[Alias]`, `extern[C]/fn[puts]` and `extern[Rust]/fn[other]`.

**Selectors from syntactic ancestry.** Selectors are built from nested outline ancestry within one file. The tests assert `mod[local]/fn[run]`, `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`, `trait[Trait]/fn[read]` and `trait[Trait]/type[Item]`. Duplicates get ordinals: `fn[repeated]#1` and `fn[repeated]#2`.

**No cross-file module resolution.**
- Nothing in the profile follows a `mod` declaration to another file.
- The tests assert `mod[external]` for `mod external;`, a node with no children, so no cross-file resolution happens.

**Impl names.**
- `impl_name` names an impl by the text of its `type` field plus the optional `trait` field.
- Tests assert `impl[Thing]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]` and `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]`, where the bracketed self type is percent-encoded.
- They also assert `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]` for a generic impl.

**Anonymous items.** Both `use_declaration` and item-position `macro_invocation` use `NameRule::Anonymous`.
- `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` asserts that `use` selectors start with `use@` and differ from each other.
- `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` asserts `^macro@[0-9a-f]{12}$` for item macros.
- The same test asserts that macros inside function bodies are not nodes.

**Documentation.** `md/reference.md` has a "Rust items" section that gives the selector spelling: examples, impl naming, and anonymous `use` and macro forms. The outline-profile table in the same file lists the kinds and how each is named, including `extern` and `extern-crate`.

No test-only gap, no unspecified behavior and no `{fixme}` needs acknowledging.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
